summary.name: VSCodium
summary.one_liner: VSCodium is a community-driven, freely licensed (MIT) binary build of Microsoft's VS Code source code, with telemetry disabled.
keywords: free software code editor linux mac windows
use_cases: Install a telemetry-free build of VS Code
Get MIT-licensed VS Code binaries instead of Microsoft's product
Install a code editor on macOS via Homebrew
Install a code editor on Windows via WinGet, Chocolatey or Scoop
Install a code editor on Linux via Snap, Flatpak, apt, dnf or AUR
summary.what_it_does: The project clones Microsoft's vscode repository and runs build scripts that produce binaries without Microsoft's customizations, such as telemetry, gallery and logo, and publishes them to GitHub releases. The binaries are licensed under MIT and the page states telemetry is disabled. The page lists many install routes: Homebrew cask on Mac, WinGet, Chocolatey and Scoop on Windows, Snap, Flatpak, Nix, AUR, Parrot OS, and deb/rpm repositories maintained by a related project for Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, RHEL, Rocky Linux and openSUSE, plus Gentoo and Funtoo ebuilds. Packages from third-party repositories are supported by those repositories' maintainers rather than the VSCodium project.
notable: Built from Microsoft's VS Code source but without Microsoft's telemetry and proprietary product customizations
Available through many package managers across macOS, Windows and Linux
Windows code signing provided by SignPath.io
caveats: Mojave users may need to right-click and choose Open the first time they launch the app, due to Apple's malware check
Package manager installs are supported by their own repositories, not by the VSCodium project
